title: EXPLORE A NEW CONSUMABLE PRODUCT WITH CHATGPT
content:
A genuinely new consumable adds product-development questions to all the normal questions of a replenishable product.

You need to understand what problem the product solves, why existing consumables do not solve it adequately, what the new product must do, and what would need to be tested before anyone should rely on it.

START WITH FUNCTION, NOT FORMULA
Do not ask ChatGPT to invent a finished food, supplement, cosmetic, chemical, or other consequential formulation and then assume it is safe. Begin with the customer problem and functional requirements. Qualified specialists may be needed to develop and test the actual product.

CONSUMABLES HAVE REPEAT EXPOSURE
Because customers may use the product repeatedly, consistency, safety, stability, storage, packaging, and instructions can matter substantially. The relevant requirements depend on the category.

INVENTION AND BUSINESS ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS
Even if a new product can technically be created, you still need to determine whether customers want it, whether it can be produced at workable economics, and whether you want to operate the resulting business.

COPY & PASTE INTO CHATGPT

Interview me to create an early development brief for a new consumable product. Ask about the intended user, problem, existing alternatives, what is missing from them, the function the product needs to perform, how it would be used, expected consumption pattern, packaging or storage constraints, and what a prototype or sample would need to prove.

Keep the discussion at product-planning level. Do not formulate or prescribe a food, supplement, cosmetic, chemical, medical, or otherwise safety-sensitive product. Identify where a qualified formulator, chemist, food scientist, engineer, laboratory, attorney, manufacturer, or other specialist may be needed.

Flag safety, stability, shelf life, ingredients or materials, testing, labeling, claims, regulation, intellectual property, manufacturing feasibility, MOQ, current quotes, and demand for independent verification. Do not claim novelty, patentability, safety, compliance, or manufacturability.

At the end give me:
- Intended user/problem
- Functional requirements
- Existing alternatives to investigate
- Important constraints
- What an early sample/prototype needs to establish
- Expertise likely needed
- Safety, regulatory, IP, manufacturing, and demand questions
- Concise product-development direction

WHERE TO GO NEXT
If the direction is specific enough to investigate seriously, continue to PDF 46. If the product turns out to be an existing category that mainly needs your branding or specifications, return to PDF 24.
